review.author: OpenPath
review.note: Candidate draft (E2a), not reviewed by an English educator (D-4). Descriptors are OpenPath's own wording. Difficulty labels are expert estimates, not empirically calibrated. Builds on 0.1.0: the 17 skeleton capabilities are unchanged; the 39 core capabilities are newly specified.

capabilities.name: Spells inflected forms correctly
capabilities.description: Spells words correctly when adding endings (-ed, -ing, -s/-es, -er/-est), applying doubling, dropping 'e' and changing 'y' to 'i'.

bands.2: Adds -s and -ing to simple words without changing the base.
bands.4: Applies doubling and silent-e rules to common one-syllable words.
bands.6: Applies the rules to two-syllable words, including stress-dependent doubling (begin → beginning).
bands.8: Handles exceptions and less common patterns reliably (panicked, travelling/traveling conventions).

misconceptions.description: Does not double the final consonant (runing, stoped).
Keeps the silent e before a vowel suffix (makeing, hopeing).
Does not change y to i (carryed, happyer).
Doubles where it should not (openning, visitted).

capabilities.name: Homophones
capabilities.description: Chooses the right spelling of words that sound the same or nearly the same (there/their/they're, its/it's, whose/who's).

bands.2: Chooses between very common pairs in simple sentences (to/two, see/sea).
bands.4: Chooses correctly among common sets in everyday writing (there/their/they're, your/you're, its/it's).
bands.6: Distinguishes less common pairs and near-homophones (principal/principle, stationary/stationery, whose/who's).
bands.8: Uses demanding homophones and near-homophones accurately (complement/compliment, affect/effect, discreet/discrete).

misconceptions.description: Confuses a contraction with a possessive (it's/its, you're/your, who's/whose).
Uses the more familiar spelling whatever the meaning (there for their).
Confuses words that sound nearly alike (accept/except, affect/effect).

capabilities.name: Morphological spelling (prefixes and suffixes)
capabilities.description: Keeps the spelling of a base word and its prefix or suffix when they are joined (unnecessary, misspell, hopeful, government, -able/-ible).

bands.2: Adds common prefixes and suffixes without changing the base (unhappy, helpful).
bands.4: Keeps both letters where a prefix meets a base with the same letter (unnatural, misspell), and spells -ful, -ly and -ment correctly.
bands.6: Chooses between -able/-ible, -tion/-sion/-ssion and -ance/-ence in common words.
bands.8: Spells less common derived words reliably, using knowledge of roots (accommodate, conscientious, irrelevant).

misconceptions.description: Drops one letter where a prefix and base meet (mispell, unecessary).
Writes -full for the suffix -ful (hopefull, carefull).
Chooses -able/-ible or -ance/-ence by sound alone.

capabilities.name: General vocabulary breadth
capabilities.description: Knows the meanings of common and moderately frequent English words; frequency band sets the difficulty.

bands.2: Knows very common everyday words (first 1,000).
bands.4: Knows most words in everyday texts (about 2,000–3,000 word families).
bands.6: Knows less frequent general words met in secondary-level reading.
bands.8: Knows low-frequency, precise general vocabulary.

misconceptions.description: Confuses a word with one that looks or sounds similar.

capabilities.name: Academic vocabulary
capabilities.description: Understands and uses the general academic words of school subjects (compare, evidence, method, factor, significant).

bands.2: Knows classroom instruction words (list, match, underline, describe).
bands.4: Knows common cross-subject words in context (compare, method, result, explain).
bands.6: Understands abstract academic words in textbooks (factor, significant, contrast, evaluate).
bands.8: Uses precise academic words accurately in their own explanations and arguments (hypothesis, implication, consequently).

misconceptions.description: Reads an academic word in an everyday sense (a 'factor' as a person, 'significant' as big).
Confuses what instruction words ask for (describe and explain, compare and contrast).

capabilities.name: Prefixes
capabilities.description: Uses prefixes to work out and form meanings (un-, re-, dis-, mis-, pre-, over-, im-/in-/il-/ir-, inter-, sub-).

bands.2: Knows un- and re- on familiar words (unhappy, redo).
bands.4: Uses common prefixes to work out meanings (disagree, misread, preview, overcook).
bands.6: Chooses the right negative prefix and uses less common prefixes (impossible, irregular, illegal; international, submarine).
bands.8: Uses prefixes in abstract and academic words to infer precise meanings (counterproductive, semi-permanent, misconception).

misconceptions.description: Uses the wrong negative prefix (unpossible, inregular, unlegal).
Confuses prefixes with similar forms (pre-/pro-, inter-/intra-, dis-/mis-).

capabilities.name: Suffixes and word class
capabilities.description: Uses suffixes to form and recognise words of different classes (-ness, -ful, -ly, -tion, -ment, -able, -ise/-ize).

bands.2: Recognises -ful, -ly and -er on familiar words.
bands.4: Chooses the right form of a word for its place in a sentence (happy/happiness/happily).
bands.6: Forms less common derivations and recognises how a suffix changes meaning.
bands.8: Handles irregular and abstract derivations (maintain → maintenance).

misconceptions.description: Uses the right word family but the wrong word class (He spoke confident).
Builds a form that does not exist (happyness, decidement).

capabilities.name: Works out meaning from context
capabilities.description: Works out the meaning of an unfamiliar word or phrase from clues in the surrounding text.

bands.2: Uses a picture or an obvious definition next to the word.
bands.4: Uses a nearby synonym, example or contrast clue in a short text.
bands.6: Combines clues across sentences in a longer, less familiar text.
bands.8: Infers precise meaning from subtle or indirect clues, including tone.

misconceptions.description: Chooses a familiar meaning of the word that does not fit the text.

capabilities.name: Multiple-meaning words
capabilities.description: Chooses the meaning of a word that fits its context when the word has several (bank, light, current, address).

bands.2: Knows two everyday meanings of very common words (a bat, to bat).
bands.4: Picks the meaning that fits the sentence for common words (light: not heavy / a lamp).
bands.6: Distinguishes subject-specific meanings of familiar words (table in maths, current in science).
bands.8: Handles less obvious and figurative senses (a sharp decline, to address a problem).

misconceptions.description: Uses the most familiar meaning whatever the context.

capabilities.name: Synonyms and antonyms
capabilities.description: Recognises words with similar or opposite meanings, and how near-synonyms differ.

bands.2: Matches very common opposites (big/small, open/close).
bands.4: Finds a synonym or antonym for common words in context (begin/start, ancient/modern).
bands.6: Chooses the synonym that fits a sentence's meaning and formality (huge, vast, immense).
bands.8: Distinguishes fine differences between near-synonyms and their effect (stubborn/determined, thrifty/stingy).

misconceptions.description: Chooses a word from the same topic rather than one with the same meaning (doctor for hospital).
Gives an opposite when asked for a similar word, or the reverse.

capabilities.name: Collocations
capabilities.description: Uses words that naturally go together (make a decision, heavy rain, take a photo, strong coffee).

bands.2: Uses very common fixed phrases (thank you very much, good morning).
bands.4: Chooses common verb–noun collocations (make a mistake, do homework, take a photo).
bands.6: Uses adjective–noun and adverb collocations (heavy traffic, deeply sorry, strong argument).
bands.8: Uses less common and academic collocations accurately (draw a conclusion, pose a question, bitterly disappointed).

misconceptions.description: Confuses make and do (do a mistake, make homework).
Builds a phrase word by word from another language (big rain, open the light).

capabilities.name: Similes and metaphors
capabilities.description: Understands what a simile or metaphor compares and what it suggests.

bands.2: Understands common simple similes (as cold as ice).
bands.4: Explains what a simile or simple metaphor compares (her voice was music).
bands.6: Interprets less familiar metaphors and the feeling they create.
bands.8: Interprets extended or layered metaphors and how they shape a text's meaning.

misconceptions.description: Reads the comparison literally.
Picks a quality the two things do not share in this context.

capabilities.name: Phrasal verbs
capabilities.description: Understands and uses verb + particle combinations (look after, give up, put off, turn down).

bands.2: Understands common phrasal verbs with literal meanings (sit down, get up).
bands.4: Understands common idiomatic phrasal verbs (look after, give up, find out).
bands.6: Chooses between similar phrasal verbs (put off, put up with, put out) and uses them in writing.
bands.8: Uses a wide range of phrasal verbs accurately, including those with several meanings (pick up, make out, bring about).

misconceptions.description: Reads the particle literally (give up as giving something upwards).
Uses the wrong particle (look for when look after is meant).

capabilities.name: Precise word choice in writing
capabilities.description: Chooses precise, varied words in their own writing.

bands.2: Uses very general words (good, nice, thing) for most meanings.
bands.4: Sometimes replaces general words with more precise ones.
bands.6: Chooses precise verbs, nouns and adjectives that suit the purpose.
bands.8: Chooses words deliberately for precision, tone and effect.

misconceptions.description: Relies on vague words (nice, thing, stuff, very good).
Uses an unfamiliar, impressive-sounding word with the wrong meaning.

capabilities.name: Plurals and countability
capabilities.description: Forms regular and irregular plurals and treats countable and uncountable nouns correctly (information, advice, furniture; many/much).

bands.2: Forms regular plurals with -s and -es (cats, boxes).
bands.4: Forms common irregular plurals (children, teeth, mice) and uses many and much with simple nouns.
bands.6: Treats common uncountable nouns correctly (advice, information, furniture, luggage).
bands.8: Handles nouns used both ways and less common plurals (a coffee / coffee; criteria, phenomena).

misconceptions.description: Adds -s to uncountable nouns (informations, advices, furnitures).
Regularises irregular plurals (childs, mouses).
Uses much with countable nouns or many with uncountable ones.

references.cbse: Determiners (quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns)

capabilities.name: Articles
capabilities.description: Chooses a, an, the or no article correctly.

bands.2: Uses a/an with simple singular countable nouns.
bands.4: Distinguishes first mention from known reference (a dog … the dog).
bands.6: Handles uncountable and general/abstract nouns (Ø information, the environment).
bands.8: Controls articles with proper nouns, idioms and generic statements consistently.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out a needed article (She is teacher).
Uses a/an with uncountable nouns (an advice).
Chooses a/an by spelling, not sound (a hour, an university).

capabilities.name: Present and past simple
capabilities.description: Forms and uses the present simple and past simple, including irregular past forms, questions and negatives.

bands.2: Uses the present simple for habits and the past simple of common regular verbs (walked, played).
bands.4: Uses common irregular past forms (went, saw, bought) and did/didn't in questions and negatives.
bands.6: Keeps tense consistent across a text and uses less common irregular forms (caught, brought, chose).
bands.8: Uses uncommon irregular forms accurately (sought, forbade, wept) and controls tense in complex narratives.

misconceptions.description: Adds -ed to irregular verbs (goed, buyed).
Uses a past form after did (Did you went?).
Shifts between present and past without reason.

capabilities.name: Progressive and perfect aspect
capabilities.description: Uses progressive and perfect forms (is doing, was doing, has done, had done) for the right meanings.

bands.2: Uses present progressive for actions happening now.
bands.4: Chooses between past simple and past progressive for an interrupted action.
bands.6: Uses present perfect versus past simple appropriately (I have lived / I lived).
bands.8: Controls past perfect and perfect progressive in complex narratives.

misconceptions.description: Uses present perfect with a finished time (I have seen him yesterday).
Uses progressive with stative verbs (I am knowing).

capabilities.name: Subject–verb agreement
capabilities.description: Makes verbs agree with their subjects, including when phrases come between them.

bands.2: Adds -s for he/she/it in the simple present.
bands.4: Agrees with plural and singular noun subjects in simple sentences.
bands.6: Agrees across intervening phrases (The box of pencils is …).
bands.8: Handles indefinite pronouns, collective nouns and inverted order.

misconceptions.description: Omits the -s for he/she/it (She go).
Agrees with the nearest noun instead of the subject (The list of names are).

capabilities.name: Modal verbs
capabilities.description: Uses modal verbs for ability, permission, possibility, obligation, advice and deduction (can, could, may, might, must, should, have to).

bands.2: Uses can and can't for ability.
bands.4: Uses must, should, can and may for obligation, advice and permission.
bands.6: Uses modals for degrees of possibility (might, could, must) and simple past modals (could have).
bands.8: Uses modals precisely for deduction and nuance (must have been, needn't have, should have).

misconceptions.description: Adds to after a modal (must to go, can to swim).
Adds -s or a past form after a modal (she cans, could went).
Confuses mustn't (not allowed) with don't have to (not necessary).

capabilities.name: Passive voice
capabilities.description: Forms and uses the passive voice (is made, was built, has been sold, will be announced).

bands.2: Recognises a simple passive with a familiar verb (The cake was eaten).
bands.4: Forms the present and past simple passive (is cleaned, was built).
bands.6: Forms passives in other tenses and with modals (has been sold, will be announced, must be done) and chooses active or passive sensibly.
bands.8: Uses passive structures deliberately for focus and formality, including reporting passives (It is said that…).

misconceptions.description: Leaves out be (The house built in 1990).
Uses the base or past form instead of the past participle (was write, was wrote).

capabilities.name: Conditionals
capabilities.description: Forms and uses conditional sentences (zero, first, second, third and mixed).

bands.2: Understands simple if-sentences about facts and routines (If it rains, we stay inside).
bands.4: Forms first conditionals (If it rains, we will stay inside).
bands.6: Forms second conditionals for unreal situations (If I had wings, I would fly).
bands.8: Forms third and mixed conditionals (If she had left earlier, she would be here now).

misconceptions.description: Uses will in the if-clause (If it will rain…).
Mixes forms from different conditionals (If I would have…).

capabilities.name: Comparatives and superlatives
capabilities.description: Forms and uses comparatives and superlatives, and comparison structures (as … as, less/fewer).

bands.2: Adds -er and -est to short adjectives (taller, tallest).
bands.4: Uses more and most with longer adjectives, and common irregular forms (better, worst).
bands.6: Uses spelling changes (bigger, happier) and structures such as as … as and not as … as.
bands.8: Compares precisely, including less/fewer, much or far + comparative, and the more …, the more ….

misconceptions.description: Uses more with -er (more taller).
Regularises irregular forms (gooder, badder).
Uses less with countable plurals (less people).

capabilities.name: Prepositions of time and place
capabilities.description: Uses prepositions of time and place accurately (in, on, at, since, for, by, until, during).

bands.2: Uses in, on and under for simple places.
bands.4: Uses at, on and in for times (at 5 o'clock, on Monday, in June) and common places.
bands.6: Uses since/for, by/until and during/while correctly.
bands.8: Chooses prepositions accurately in less common expressions (in time / on time, at the end / in the end).

misconceptions.description: Confuses in, on and at for times or places (on 5 o'clock, in Monday).
Uses since with a length of time or for with a starting point (since two hours).

capabilities.name: Questions
capabilities.description: Forms yes/no, wh-, subject and indirect questions, and question tags.

bands.2: Forms simple yes/no questions with be and can (Is she…? Can you…?).
bands.4: Forms wh- questions with do, does and did (Where do you live?).
bands.6: Forms subject questions and question tags (Who broke it? It's late, isn't it?).
bands.8: Forms indirect and embedded questions correctly (Could you tell me where the station is?).

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the auxiliary or the inversion (Where you live?).
Inverts inside an embedded question (Tell me where is the station).

capabilities.name: Relative clauses
capabilities.description: Uses relative clauses with who, which, that, whose and where, defining and non-defining.

bands.2: Understands simple who and which clauses after a noun.
bands.4: Joins two sentences with who, which or that.
bands.6: Uses whose and where, and punctuates non-defining clauses with commas.
bands.8: Uses relative clauses with prepositions and reduced forms accurately (the house in which…, the man sitting there).

misconceptions.description: Uses which for people (the boy which…).
Repeats the pronoun inside the clause (the book that I read it).

capabilities.name: Reported speech
capabilities.description: Reports statements, questions, commands and requests, with the right tense, pronoun, word-order and time changes.

bands.2: Understands simple reported statements (She said she was tired).
bands.4: Reports statements with tense and pronoun changes (He said, 'I am hungry.' → He said he was hungry).
bands.6: Reports questions, commands and requests (asked if…, told me to…) with word-order and time changes.
bands.8: Uses a range of reporting verbs accurately (advised, denied, suggested) with the right patterns.

misconceptions.description: Keeps the original tense where it should change.
Keeps question word order in a reported question (asked where was I going).
Keeps the speaker's pronouns (He said I am hungry).

references.cbse: Reported Speech (commands and requests, statements, questions)

capabilities.name: Capitalisation
capabilities.description: Uses capital letters for sentence starts, I, names, places, days, months, languages and titles, and not elsewhere.

bands.2: Uses a capital at the start of a sentence and for I and names.
bands.4: Capitalises days, months, places and languages (Monday, July, Chennai, Tamil).
bands.6: Capitalises titles, organisations and proper adjectives, and avoids capitals on common nouns.
bands.8: Applies capitalisation conventions consistently, including in headings, quotations and less common proper nouns.

misconceptions.description: Writes proper nouns in lower case (chennai, monday).
Capitalises common nouns for emphasis (my School, the River).

capabilities.name: End punctuation
capabilities.description: Ends sentences with the right mark: full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.

bands.2: Ends a simple statement with a full stop.
bands.4: Uses question marks and exclamation marks correctly, including in short dialogue.
bands.6: Punctuates indirect questions (without a question mark) and longer sentences correctly.
bands.8: Uses end punctuation consistently and deliberately, including inside quotations.

misconceptions.description: Puts a question mark after an indirect question (I wonder where he is?).
Ends a direct question with a full stop.

capabilities.name: Commas
capabilities.description: Uses commas for lists, after introductory parts, around extra information and before conjunctions joining clauses.

bands.2: Separates items in a simple list.
bands.4: Uses a comma after an introductory word or phrase.
bands.6: Places commas around non-essential information and before a joining conjunction.
bands.8: Uses commas precisely to avoid ambiguity, and avoids unnecessary ones.

misconceptions.description: Joins two complete sentences with only a comma.
Omits the comma after a long introductory part.

capabilities.name: Apostrophes
capabilities.description: Uses apostrophes for contractions and possession, and not for plain plurals.

bands.2: Uses apostrophes in very common contractions (don't, I'm).
bands.4: Uses 's for singular possession (the girl's bag) and apostrophes in contractions.
bands.6: Uses s' for plural possession and its/it's correctly (the girls' bags).
bands.8: Handles irregular plural and joint possession, and avoids apostrophes in plain plurals (children's; mangoes, not mango's).

misconceptions.description: Adds an apostrophe to a plain plural (mango's for sale).
Writes it's for the possessive its.
Puts the apostrophe in the wrong place for plural possession (the girl's bags for several girls).

capabilities.name: Complete sentences, not fragments
capabilities.description: Writes complete sentences, each with a subject and a main verb, and avoids accidental fragments.

bands.2: Writes simple complete sentences with a subject and verb.
bands.4: Recognises and fixes obvious fragments (Because it was raining.).
bands.6: Avoids fragments in longer writing, including -ing and which fragments.
bands.8: Uses fragments only deliberately, for effect.

misconceptions.description: Writes a subordinate clause on its own as a sentence.
Leaves out the main verb (My brother in the garden.).

capabilities.name: Avoids run-on sentences and comma splices
capabilities.description: Ends or joins independent clauses correctly when writing.

bands.2: Separates two short, simple statements with a full stop.
bands.4: Correctly joins or separates clauses in everyday writing, most of the time.
bands.6: Controls sentence boundaries in longer writing, including with transitions.
bands.8: Uses boundary choices (semicolon, dash, subordination) deliberately for effect.

misconceptions.description: Joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
Runs two independent clauses together with no punctuation.
Splits dependent clauses off as sentences.

capabilities.name: Coordination
capabilities.description: Joins ideas with coordinating words (and, but, or, so, yet, nor) and paired forms (either … or, both … and).

bands.2: Joins two simple ideas with and or but.
bands.4: Chooses and, but, or and so to show the right link.
bands.6: Uses yet, nor and paired forms (either … or, both … and), and avoids long chains of and.
bands.8: Balances coordination and subordination for clarity and rhythm.

misconceptions.description: Strings many clauses together with and.
Uses a coordinator that shows the wrong link (but where so is meant).

capabilities.name: Subordination
capabilities.description: Joins ideas with subordinating words (because, although, when, unless, so that) to show how they relate.

bands.2: Joins two ideas with because or when.
bands.4: Chooses a subordinator that shows the right relationship (although vs because).
bands.6: Varies position and type of subordinate clauses for clarity.
bands.8: Uses subordination to manage complex relationships between several ideas.

misconceptions.description: Uses a joining word that states the wrong relationship (because for contrast).
Leaves a subordinate clause without a main clause.

capabilities.name: Embedding (relative and participle phrases)
capabilities.description: Combines ideas by embedding relative clauses and participle phrases.

bands.2: Understands a sentence with a short describing phrase (the girl in the red dress).
bands.4: Combines two sentences using who or which.
bands.6: Combines sentences using participle phrases (Running for the bus, she dropped her bag) without dangling them.
bands.8: Embeds several ideas in one controlled sentence for concision.

misconceptions.description: The participle phrase does not describe the subject (Walking home, the rain started).
Packs in so many embedded parts that the sentence loses its meaning.

capabilities.name: Connectives and transitions
capabilities.description: Uses connectives and transitions that show how sentences relate (however, therefore, for example, as a result).

bands.2: Uses first, then and next to order events.
bands.4: Uses common connectives for addition, contrast and result (also, however, so).
bands.6: Chooses connectives that show the exact relationship (therefore, despite this, for instance).
bands.8: Uses a range of transitions to guide a reader through an argument.

misconceptions.description: Uses a connective that shows the wrong relationship (however where therefore is meant).
Starts most sentences with a connective.

capabilities.name: Locates explicit detail
capabilities.description: Finds information stated directly in a text.

bands.2: Finds a stated fact in a short, simple text.
bands.4: Finds details in a text of several paragraphs, ignoring distractors.
bands.6: Locates and matches details expressed in different words from the question.
bands.8: Locates precise details in dense or complex texts.

misconceptions.description: Picks an option because it repeats words from the text, not because it answers the question.

capabilities.name: Sequences events
capabilities.description: Puts the events of a text in the order they happened.

bands.2: Orders three events in a short story.
bands.4: Orders events in a text of several paragraphs, using time words.
bands.6: Orders events when the text tells them out of order (flashbacks, later explanations).
bands.8: Reconstructs complex or interleaved timelines.

misconceptions.description: Assumes events happened in the order they are mentioned.

capabilities.name: Infers feelings and motives
capabilities.description: Infers characters' feelings, motives and attitudes from what they say and do.

bands.2: Names an obvious feeling shown by an action (crying → sad).
bands.4: Infers a motive from a clear sequence of actions.
bands.6: Infers mixed or changing feelings from dialogue and detail.
bands.8: Infers subtle, ironic or unstated motives and attitudes.

misconceptions.description: Answers with what the text states rather than what it implies.

capabilities.name: Cause and effect
capabilities.description: Identifies and infers causes and effects in a text.

bands.2: Finds a cause stated with because.
bands.4: Links a cause and effect stated in different sentences.
bands.6: Infers causes and effects that are not directly stated.
bands.8: Distinguishes multiple and indirect causes, and causes from coincidences.

misconceptions.description: Treats an earlier event as the cause just because it came first.
Gives the effect as the cause, or the reverse.

capabilities.name: Identifies the main idea
capabilities.description: Identifies what a text or paragraph is mainly about, as distinct from its details.

bands.2: Identifies the topic of a short text.
bands.4: Chooses the main idea of a paragraph over a detail.
bands.6: States the main idea of a multi-paragraph text.
bands.8: Identifies implicit main ideas and the writer's central claim.

misconceptions.description: Chooses an interesting detail as the main idea.

capabilities.name: Summarises
capabilities.description: Identifies the key points of a text and condenses them, leaving out minor detail.

bands.2: Retells the main event of a short text.
bands.4: Chooses the summary that covers the main points without small details.
bands.6: Identifies the key points of a multi-paragraph text and leaves out examples.
bands.8: Condenses a complex text accurately, keeping the writer's line of argument.

misconceptions.description: Includes minor details or examples.
Covers only part of the text.
Adds their own opinion to the summary.

capabilities.name: Non-fiction text structure
capabilities.description: Recognises how non-fiction is organised (sequence, description, compare and contrast, cause and effect, problem and solution) and uses headings.

bands.2: Uses a title and pictures to tell what a text is about.
bands.4: Recognises sequence and description structures, and uses headings to find information.
bands.6: Recognises compare-and-contrast, cause-and-effect and problem-and-solution structures.
bands.8: Explains how a text's structure supports its purpose.

misconceptions.description: Judges structure by the topic instead of by how the text is organised.

capabilities.name: Purpose and audience
capabilities.description: Identifies a text's purpose and intended audience, and how its language suits them.

bands.2: Tells whether a text is a story, a letter or instructions.
bands.4: Identifies the main purpose (to inform, persuade, entertain or instruct).
bands.6: Identifies the intended audience and how the language is chosen for it.
bands.8: Explains mixed or hidden purposes (an advertisement written to look like news).

misconceptions.description: Decides the purpose from the topic instead of from what the text does.

capabilities.name: Fact and opinion
capabilities.description: Distinguishes facts, opinions and opinions presented as facts.

bands.2: Tells a simple fact from a simple opinion (Cats have four legs / Cats are the best pets).
bands.4: Recognises opinion words (best, should, I think) in short texts.
bands.6: Distinguishes facts, opinions and claims presented as facts.
bands.8: Evaluates how a writer blends fact and opinion to persuade.

misconceptions.description: Treats a confidently stated opinion as a fact.
Treats any sentence containing a number as a fact.

capabilities.name: Responds to the task
capabilities.description: Writes what the task asks for: the right purpose, content and length for the reader.

bands.2: Writes a few relevant words or sentences on the topic.
bands.4: Addresses the main parts of a simple task.
bands.6: Addresses all parts of the task with relevant, developed content.
bands.8: Fulfils the task fully and precisely, anticipating the reader's needs.

misconceptions.description: Writes about the topic but does not do what the task asks.

capabilities.name: Develops ideas with detail
capabilities.description: Develops ideas with relevant detail, examples and explanation.

bands.2: Lists ideas with little detail.
bands.4: Adds a reason or an example to some ideas.
bands.6: Develops each main idea with relevant detail, examples or explanation.
bands.8: Develops ideas in depth, choosing the most telling detail.

misconceptions.description: Lists ideas without explaining or supporting them.
Adds detail that does not support the idea.

references.cbse: Writing: analytical paragraph on a given map, chart, graph or cues

capabilities.name: Paragraphing
capabilities.description: Groups sentences into paragraphs, each with a clear focus.

bands.2: Writes in one block.
bands.4: Uses paragraphs for the main parts (opening, body, ending).
bands.6: Each paragraph has a clear focus, often with a topic sentence.
bands.8: Paragraphing supports the argument or narrative deliberately.

misconceptions.description: Writes everything as one paragraph.
Starts a new paragraph for every sentence.

capabilities.name: Logical sequencing
capabilities.description: Orders ideas and events logically so a reader can follow them.

bands.2: Puts events in a sensible order.
bands.4: Orders ideas so the reader can follow them.
bands.6: Orders points logically, with clear links between them.
bands.8: Arranges complex content in the most effective order for the purpose.

misconceptions.description: Moves between ideas and back again without a clear order.

capabilities.name: Narrative writing
capabilities.description: Writes stories with a clear structure, characters and setting.

bands.2: Writes a few connected sentences about events.
bands.4: Writes a story with a beginning, middle and end.
bands.6: Develops character, setting, and a clear problem and resolution.
bands.8: Controls pace, viewpoint and detail for effect.

misconceptions.description: Stops the story without resolving its problem.
Lists events without connecting them into a story.

capabilities.name: Persuasive writing
capabilities.description: Writes to persuade: a clear position supported by reasons and evidence, aware of the reader.

bands.2: States an opinion.
bands.4: Gives an opinion with reasons.
bands.6: Supports a clear position with reasons and evidence, and addresses the reader.
bands.8: Builds a structured argument, answers counter-arguments and persuades through language.

misconceptions.description: States opinions without reasons or evidence.
Does not acknowledge any other point of view where the task needs it.

capabilities.name: Functional writing (letters, emails, notices)
capabilities.description: Writes letters, emails, notices and messages with the right conventions, purpose and register.

bands.2: Writes a short message with a greeting.
bands.4: Uses the main conventions of an informal letter, email or notice.
bands.6: Writes formal letters and notices with the right layout, purpose and register.
bands.8: Writes precise, well-judged functional texts for varied real purposes.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out expected parts (greeting, subject, closing, date of a notice).
Uses informal language in a formal letter or notice.

references.cbse: Writing: formal letter based on a given situation

capabilities.name: Audience and register
capabilities.description: Adjusts formality and tone to the audience and purpose.

bands.2: Writes the same way for every reader.
bands.4: Makes some changes for formal or informal readers.
bands.6: Keeps a suitable register throughout a piece (a formal letter as against a message to a friend).
bands.8: Adjusts register precisely for purpose, audience and effect.

misconceptions.description: Mixes formal and informal language (Dear Sir, hope ur fine).
Uses text-message spellings in formal writing.

capabilities.name: Grammatical accuracy in writing
capabilities.description: Writes with grammatical accuracy in their own extended writing.

bands.2: Simple sentences, frequent errors that sometimes block meaning.
bands.4: Errors are noticeable but rarely block meaning.
bands.6: Mostly accurate, with errors in more complex structures.
bands.8: Accurate across a range of structures; errors are rare slips.

misconceptions.description: Omits the -s for he/she/it.
Shifts tense without reason.
Leaves out needed articles.

capabilities.name: Spelling in writing
capabilities.description: Spells accurately in their own extended writing.

bands.2: Many common words misspelled.
bands.4: Common words mostly correct; errors in longer words.
bands.6: Few errors, mainly in less common words.
bands.8: Almost no errors.

misconceptions.description: Spells by sound (becos, freind).

capabilities.name: Asks and answers questions, takes turns
